chain.label: Discrete dirty white spot manufacturing anomaly in HPT stage 2 disk
chain.trigger: an internal subsurface manufacturing anomaly that was most likely not detectable during production inspections and subsequent in-service inspections

chain.label: Uncontained rupture (rotor burst) of HPT stage 2 disk
chain.trigger: the failure of the HPT stage 2 disk

caused_by.evidence: The HPT stage 2 disk failed because of low-cycle fatigue cracks that initiated from an internal subsurface manufacturing anomaly

chain.label: Fuel feed line severed and right wing fuel tank breached, causing fuel-fed fire
chain.trigger: severed the main engine fuel feed line and breached the right main wing fuel tank, releasing fuel that resulted in a fire on the right side of the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the failure of the HPT stage 2 disk, which severed the main engine fuel feed line and breached the right main wing fuel tank, releasing fuel that resulted in a fire

chain.label: Engine fire checklist did not differentiate ground vs. in-flight operations
chain.trigger: the engine fire checklist did not differentiate between an engine fire in flight and an engine fire while the airplane was on the ground and did not include a step...to shut down the unaffected engine or perform the evacuation checklist sooner

chain.label: Lack of communication between flight and cabin crews after the airplane stopped
chain.trigger: none of the flight attendants activated the signaling system, and only two of the seven flight attendants attempted (unsuccessfully) to communicate with the flight crew using the interphone system

chain.label: Flight attendant deviated from procedure, evacuating passengers from left overwing exit while left engine still ran
chain.trigger: another flight attendant stationed on the left side of the airplane assessed the conditions outside the airplane yet opened the left overwing exit while the engine was still operating

caused_by.evidence: the flight attendants had already initiated the evacuation...due to the severity of the fire on the right side of the airplane
Contributing to the delay in shutting down the left engine was (1) the lack of a separate checklist procedure for Boeing 767 airplanes that specifically addressed engine fires on the ground
(2) the lack of communication between the flight and cabin crews

chain.label: Passenger seriously injured by jet blast after evacuating via left overwing exit
chain.trigger: the passenger stood up to get away from the airplane but was knocked down by the jet blast coming from the left engine

caused_by.evidence: The one serious injury that resulted during the evacuation occurred after a passenger evacuated using the left overwing exit
